en.value: Somatostatin is a hormone secreted by which of the following?

options.prompt: Beta cells of Islets of Langerhans of Pancreas
Alpha cells of Islets of Langerhans of
Delta cells of Islets of Langerhans of

english.explanation: Somatostatin (SST) is a harmone secreted by delta cells of islets of langerhans of pancreas. It regulate a larger no of physiological functions & inhibit the secretion of insulin glucagon from adjacent cells. Glucagon is a harmone secreted by alpha (α) cells of Islets of Langerhans of Pancreas. Insluin is a harmone secreted by Beta (β) cells of Islets of Langerhans of Pancreas.

en.value: Cristae are the folds of inner membrane present in which of the following cells organelle?

english.explanation: Cristae are the folds in the inner membrane of mitochondria. To increase the capacity of the mitochondrion to synthesize ATP, the inner membrane is folded to form Cristae. These folds allow a much greater amount of electron transport chain and ATP synthase to be packed into the mitochondrion. These folds allow for increased surface area for chemical reaction.

en.value: Which of the following devices is used to study the electrical activity of human brain?

english.explanation: The EEG (Electroencephalogram) device is used to measure the electrical activity of the human brain. * The brain cells communicate with each other through electrical impulses, this process remains active even in the sleep. * The EEG is used to diagnose several disorders like- epilepsy, brain tumour, brain inflammation, stroke etc. * The EEG is also used to confirm if a person in a persistent comma is brain dead or not. * ECG-Electrical signal from heart Electrocardiography. * EMG-Electromyography is diagnostic procedure to assess the health of muscles and the nerve cells that control them.

en.value: Which of the following are Omnivorous organisms?

english.explanation: Omnivorous : These organisms obtain food by feeding on both plants as well as animals. Example : Humans, Bears, Birds etc. Carnivorous: Organisms feeding only on animals. Example - Pitcher plant, Lion, Jackals, Tigers etc. Herbivorous : Organisms feeding only on plants. Example : Cow, Rabbit, Pig etc.

en.value: Fertilization in human female occurs in which of the following parts?

english.explanation: * Fertilization in human female takes place at ampullary isthemic junction in fallopian tube. * Attachment of embryo takes place at endometrial lining of uterus. * Cervix is the junction of uterus and vaginal canal.

en.value: Which of the following Vertebrates are essentially Ureotelic?

english.explanation: * Ureotelics : Which excrete urea as their excretory product. en.value: Which of the following is known as the middle man of the body?

english.explanation: * Lymph is the middle man of body because it mediates exchange of oxygen, hormones & food material to the cells with CO2 & other metabolic wastes. * It is pale yellow coloured liquid functions same as blood. * Blood & lymph both are connecting tissues. * Veins are the tubes through with impure blood transport. * Nerves transmit the electrical signal produced due to stimuli.

en.value: Parkinson's diseases affects which of the following organ in human beings?

english.explanation: Parkinson's disease damages the nerve cells of brain due to which dopamine level drop. It occurs due to impairment or death of nerve cells present in the brain that are responsible for the control & co-ordination of the body. the symptoms of this disease include tremors or shaking of the hands & legs, difficulty while walking, impairment of the body posture, difficulty in speaking etc.

en.value: Which of the following hormones is released during parturition in female human beings?

english.explanation: Oxytocin is released during parturition. Parturition is the process of giving birth to the child. * Oxytocin also released during sex, orgasm, breastfeeding. Oxytocin causes the contractions and relaxations during parturition. * Prolactin–stimulates breasts to grow in size and producing milk during and after pregnancy. * Glucagon contract to insulin to increase glucose level in blood. * Estrogen regulates menstrual cycle and is important for promoting pregnancy.

en.value: The hair pin like structure which is a part of Nephron is :

english.explanation: * Hair pin like structure which is the part of nephron is known as loop of Henle. * Nephron is the structural and function unit of kidneys. The loop of Henle is a hair pin like structure present between Proximal Nephron (PCT) and Distal Nephron (DCT). * The loop of Henle has two limbs the descending limb and the ascending limb. * The main function of Henle's loop is to selectively reabsorb water and other important salts like NaCl, this makes the urine more concentrated.

en.value: Regeneration is seen in which of the following organisms?

english.explanation: Both Hydra and Planaria shows regeneration, but the examiner has considered planaria as the correct option in the official answer key. Hydra is a freshwater polyp that has a remarkable property to regenerate. It has the ability to re-grow the body parts which have been damaged and similar is the case with planaria. Both Hydra and Planaria use regeneration as a mode of producing new organisms.

en.value: Miller-Urey experiment is associated with which of the following?

english.explanation: Two scientists S.L. Miller and H.C. Urey conducted an experiment in the year 1953 and proved the theory of chemical evolution. In this experiment CH4, NH3, H2O (Vapour) & H2 (gas) were used in a setup with heat source. The theory of chemical evolution was proposed by Oparin and Haldane. According to this theory, the first form of life could have come from pre-existing non- living organic molecules (e.g. - RNA, protein etc) and that formation of life was preceded by chemical evolution, i.e. the formation diverse organic molecules from inorganic constituents. The conditions on earth at the time were - high temperature volcanic stroms, reducing atmosphere containing CH4, NH3 etc.

en.value: Which of the following blood vessels supply the blood to the Liver?

english.explanation: Hepatic artery primarily is soft oxygenated blood vessel that supplies oxygen - rich blood to the liver, duodenum and pancreas. The common hepatic artery is located in the abdomen, near the lower portion of T12 vertebra. Hepatic portal vein also delivers the deoxygenated blood from intestine to liver.

en.value: What is the approximate total number of nucleotides in a human genome?

english.explanation: The human genome represents the entire set of nucleic acid sequences present in the 23 pair of chromosomes in human cell. There are approximately 3 billion nucleotides present in the human genome.

english.explanation: Ecological balance is the maintenance of equilibrium in an ecosystem. en.value: Where the headquarters of International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural resources (IUCN) located?

english.explanation: IUCN head quarters is located in Gland, Switzerland. It is an international organization working in the field of nature conservation and sustainable use of natural resources. It is involved in data gathering and analysis, research, field projects, advocacy, lobbying and education. The IUCN compiled and published the IUCN Red List which assesses the conservation status of species worldwide. IUCN Red List of Threatened species founded in 1965 with the aim to spread awareness among the masses about the extiction of species and the need for conservation. International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), was established on 5 October, 1948 in France.

english.explanation: * Vacuoles are surrounded by a membrane called tonoplast. The vital role of the vacuole is to provide support against the pressure of the cell wall. * Ribosomes do not have any membrane. * Plastids – Double membrane bound. * Lysosomes is known as suicidal bag of cell.

en.value: Which of the following is Conventional source of energy?

english.explanation: * Conventional Sources.–The sources of energy which are being used from old times eg. coal, fossil fuels, CNG, LPG etc. * Non-conventional sources.–Sources of energy which are discovered newly a substitutes of conventional sources to reduce pollute & other parameters eg. Solar energy, Wind energy, Hydro power, Tidal energy etc.

en.value: Which of the following ecological pyramid is always upright?

english.explanation: Pyramid of energy is the fundamental of all and denotes the total amount of energy at each trophic level. It is always upright and vertical. Then, we also know about the 10% law by Lindeman (during the transfer of energy from one trophic level to another only 10% energy is stored) so food chains are generally short with few trophic levels as only 10% of energy is transferred to higher trophic level, rest of the energy is lost to the environment.

en.value: Which of the following global convention was formed to regulate the import and export of hazardous chemicals?

english.explanation: * Rotterdam convention was signed in the year 1998 and came into effect in 2004. It is a multilateral environmental agreement to promote shared responsibilities in relation to the importation of hazardous chemicals. * The Montreal Protocol on substances the deplete the ozone layer (9th Montreal Protocol) is an International agreement made in 1987. * The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty to the United Nations Framework Convention on climate change. Kyoto Protocol was adopted in Kyoto, Japan. It is an international treaty that aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. * Tokyo convention acts on onboard air craft. It is applicable to offences against penal law and to any acts jeopardizing the safety of the persons or property on board civilian aircraft while in flight and engage the international air navigation.

en.value: Which of the following is an example of Mutualism?

english.explanation: Mutualism is referred to as the interspecific interaction in which both the interacting species are benefited. Algae and fungi remain in a close association where the fungus helps in the absorption of nutrients and provides protection while algae or cyanobacteria prepares the food. This association is called "Lichen". Barnacles and Whales, orchid and large trees, sea anemone and crab are example of commensalism, where one species is benefitted while the other is neither benefitted nor harmed.

en.value: Which of the following diseases is caused due to contamination of drinking water?

english.explanation: Typhoid- Contamination of drinking water (Salmonella typhi) * T.B. – Inhaling droplets from infected person (Mycobacterium tuberculosis). * Human Immunodeficiency Virus – (HIV) – Blood transfusion, unprotected sex (Virus) * Leprosy- Long term and repeated contact with diseased person (Mycobacterium laprae)

english.explanation: * Hydrophytes – Plants adopted to grow in water rich area origin e.g. Eichhornia, Trapa, lotus etc. Xerophytes– Plants that are adapted to survive in little amount of water. e.g. cactus, pineapple, Acacia etc. * Epiphytes – Plants that grows on the truns or branch of any higher tree. They draw their food and moisture from air. * Halophytes – Plants adapted to grow in saline soil or water. e.g. mangroves etc.

en.value: The Chemical distinction between two adjacent Ecosystems is known as?

english.explanation: Ecocline is a term used in ecology which is defined as the physio-chemical gradient of a characteristic of a species in a specific geographical range. When there is no clear boundary between two ecosystems, there is a gradation. It is the result of an associated community and complex environmental gradients interacting. A wetland is an example of an ecocline because it is a gradual transition from a terrestrial to an aquatic ecosystem.

en.value: Which of the following pollutant is a component of acid rains?

english.explanation: HNO3, H2SO4, H2CO3 are the main components of acid rain. Acid rain is the result of several sulphur and nitrogen oxide pollutants in air. It is all due to burning of forest, fuels & volcanic activity.

en.value: Rearing of earth worms is associated with which of the following?

en.value: Solubility of potassium chloride in water is due to :

english.explanation: As potassium chloride (KCl) dissolves in water, the ions are hydrated. The polar water molecules are attracted by the charges on the K+ and Cl– ions Ion-dipole forces attract the positive (hydrogen) of the polar water molecules to the negative chloride ions at the surface of the solid, and they attract the negative (Oxygen) ends to the positive potassium ions. The water molecules penetrate between individual K+ and Cl– ions and surround them, reducing YCT DSSSB TGT Natural Science 29.09.2018 S-II 47 YCT the strong interionic forces that bind the ions together and letting them move off into solution as solvated ions. So, solubility of potassium chloride in water is due to ion-dipole interactions.

en.value: Which of the following (referred to a spherical mirror) depends on whether the rays are paraxial or not?

english.explanation: Paraxial rays are the light rays close to the principal axis. The focuses of the spherical mirror for paraxial rays are different from the focus for marginal rays. So, the focus depends on whether the rays are paraxial or marginal. The pole, radius of curvature and the principal axis of a spherical mirror do not depend on paraxial or marginal rays. Focus is the place where parallel beam of light to the principal axis meets after reflection. If the beam is not considered to be paraxial, the position of image would change after reflection.

en.value: A convex lens is made of material having refractive index 1.2. Both the surfaces of the lens are convex. If it is dipped into water (µ= 1.33), it will behave like :

english.explanation: The µ of the convex lens in greater than air so it will act as a convergent lens in the air. When it is dipped in water its µ is less than water. Now, the rays entering and exiting the lens will bend toward or away from the normal in an opposite direction then when the lens was placed in air. So, the convergent lens in the air will now behave as a divergent lens in water.

en.value: What is the significant and key factor in the ecosystem ?

english.explanation: The energy flow is one of the significant and key factors in the Ecosystem. The term Ecosystem was coined by sir A.G. Tansley (1935). The four functional units or key factors of an Ecosystem are – (i) Productivity (ii) Decomposition (iii) Energy Flow (iv) Nutrient Cycling Energy flow – Except for the deep sea hydrothermal vents, Sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth.

en.value: "Readers look at the organization of the text and ideas without relating it to their prior knowledge or experience" which of the reading models does this define ?

english.explanation: In Bottom-up reading model readers look at the organization of the text and ideas without relating is to their prior knowledge or experience. According to Browne (1998), this model describes reading as a process that starts with the learner's knowledge of letters, sounds and words and how these words are formed to make sentences. This model is called part to whole model because it goes from partial to whole knowledge. This model is so effective in the early childhood, especially students as young learners. It's effective because the emphasis here is on the letters, recognition of their shapes and reading individual words. However, this model has many disadvantages if used for higher levels since it forgets the reader's expectations, experience and attitudes. Furthermore, it doesn't pay attention to the context since it only encourages remembering.
